summary: Core repair and customer interface, package P3 (CORE-UX-DESIGN.md section 4): a pure, read-time review overlay (studio/validation/review_view.py) that recomputes, over the CURRENT decisions and member answers, the combination gates the engine computes once over its own active set - the diagnostic-base rule (services.base_included and its base_included question) and the CMS PFS endoscopic-family check (pfs.endoscopic_base) - and every gate and reader that reads a proposal's status or actions reads it (review._actions/_allowed/approve_withheld_by/record_decision, readiness/_assessment_blockers, coding_completeness, _review_state/refresh_state, serializers._proposal_json, the report snapshot, review.effective_view for the customer API, review.approved_items for the approved export). The base rule and the endoscopic-family inputs are extracted from engine._encounter/_proposal into functions the engine itself calls, so there is one implementation. A structured distinct-lesion modifier review (options 59 or XS, never both, never prefilled) is recomputed over the effective set at read time; the reviewer may choose one modifier per approval, stored on Decision.modifiers (migration 0009_cux_review, additive, database default '[]'). The member-answer effect (P5's data, P3's rule) is wired through review._member_answers, which returns [] in this package.
engine_output: BYTE-IDENTICAL. The engine's AssessmentResult (every proposal's bucket, status, checks with their details, clarifications, modifier_considerations strings, fingerprint, support; every encounter check, question and the completeness record) is unchanged on every input: the extracted base rule, the extracted base_included check/question builder and the distinct-lesion helper return exactly what the inline code returned, and _service_considerations still renders the same strings from the structured form. Nothing new is stored by the engine: the structured modifier review exists only in the read-time overlay view.
movements_note: H2 (freeze): NONE. No file the request side reads is touched (studio/gi/context.py, studio/gi/sections.py and every constant they read are unchanged), so NEW-SEND = NEW-TAKE = 0 and every request is byte-identical. studio/validation/engine.py, checks.py (new modifier-review helpers only) and review.py are read only by the assess child and the review layer.
replay_note: H1: python -m ops.gi4.replay --fixtures --base c9f20a148 --head <P3 head> must print no difference in any member state of any regression document (h4-01..h4-06, h2-08, h2-10): the overlay is not read by the assess child, and the engine extraction is byte-identical.
battery_note: H4: python -m ops.gi4.battery --base c9f20a148 --head <P3 head> --declare this file must show 0 movements and 0 new violations. The battery reads engine output, which does not move; the overlay changes statuses only at read time after a reviewer decision or a member answer, which no battery row has.

regression.h4-02: no movement in any member state
regression.h4-03: no movement in any member state

regression.h4-06: no movement in any member state
regression.h2-08: no movement in any member state

overlay.positive_control: With no decisions and no member answers the overlay reproduces every stored proposal status, every stored check (id, label, status, detail, source) and every stored open proposal-scoped question byte for byte, on every proposal of every battery row and every regression document in every member state (DB-free test), and on the D14 shapes of R3 2.3 (box_misread, denied, selected). The operator API (serializers._proposal_json), readiness, coding completeness, the encounter state and both report renders are therefore unchanged for every encounter with no decision and no answer.
overlay.effective_set: selected proposals without a current REJECT, plus excluded reinstatable proposals with a current REINSTATE or APPROVE, minus proposals a member answer makes detail_unavailable (none in this package)
recomputed_after_decisions: services.base_included check and base_included question on a base code (held iff another code of the effective set of its family covers an intervention of the same documented service, or that service documents a performed, reportable, non-bundled act: the engine's own rule, unchanged); added when newly held, released when no longer held, re-worded when the codes it names change

pfs.endoscopic_base on every decidable code that carries it, from the assessment's own retrieval facts (kept as stored, and marked not recomputed, when the retrieval does not carry the PFS row of every code whose pfs.presence passed)
review.reinstatement on a reinstated code the overlay newly holds (its stored waits plus the added question)
overlay.D14: Reinstating 45385 beside a selected 45378 holds 45378 at read time (needs_clarification, approve withheld by services.base_included, question 'Is 45378 reported separately from 45385 for this examination?'); an APPROVE already recorded on 45378 becomes a readiness blocker until revoked, so the reviewed report waits. Rejecting the therapeutic code releases the base only per the engine's own rule (a documented performed reportable act keeps it held). The same holds for a reinstated base beside a selected therapeutic code.
not_recomputed: separate_em / em.same_day_procedure on an E/M when a same-day procedure is rejected (kept: a hold is never released here; recorded limit)

every other per-code check (scope, evidence, routing, service.status, evidence.support, required facts, pfs.presence, mue.units, units.duplicate, participants.*) - none depends on another proposal's decision

modifier_review.moves: NOTHING STORED. The engine's modifier_considerations strings are byte-identical (they are rendered from the same structured distinct-lesion reading). The overlay view gains a read-time modifier_review per proposal: {kind: 'distinct_lesion', codes, lesions, options: ['59', 'XS'], text, sources: [{key, title, release, section, page}]}, present only while another code of the effective set accounts for an act on a different documented lesion of the same service, and dropped when that code leaves the effective set. Its sources cite only the dated CMS claims-manual passage the assessment's own retrieval carries (Pub. 100-04 ch. 12, item 13 example) and only for the 45380/45385 pair it describes; its text says NCCI procedure-to-procedure edits and payer modifier policy are not checked and that no modifier is added unless the reviewer chooses one.
modifier_review.operator_report: unchanged for every encounter whose decisions carry no chosen modifier and whose checks no decision recomputed; a chosen modifier adds one line under its decision; a recomputed check adds one note line

decision_modifiers: Decision.modifiers (JSONField, default list, database default '[]'::jsonb): the reviewer's ONE chosen modifier on an APPROVE ('59' or 'XS'), only when the overlay offers a modifier review for that proposal; [] otherwise. Never prefilled, never both, never a free list. Carried with the decision onto a same-fingerprint proposal; an approval whose chosen modifier the current view no longer offers becomes a readiness blocker until revoked.
